articles.body_markdown:
A person being accused, arrested, charged or convicted does not describe the same legal status. A responsible account names the event that actually occurred and links the relevant record.

The following are introductory descriptions, not advice about an individual case. Procedure can depend on the proceeding and applicable law. The BNSS itself includes savings for specified proceedings pending under the earlier criminal procedure code, so an old case should not automatically be relabelled as a new-code case. [1](https://www.mha.gov.in/sites/default/files/2024-04/250884_2_english_01042024.pdf#page=156)

## From allegation to a case before a court

An **allegation** is a claim that someone did something. Calling it an allegation does not establish that it is true or false.

An **FIR**, or First Information Report, records information in the criminal-law process concerning a cognizable offence. It is not a judgment of guilt. **Arrest** concerns taking a person into custody; it does not itself decide the accusation. [2](https://www.mha.gov.in/sites/default/files/2024-04/250884_2_english_01042024.pdf#page=52)

A **police report or chargesheet** follows investigation in the relevant procedural setting. Do not confuse it with a court's decision to frame a charge. The BNSS separately provides for a police report on completion of investigation and for court procedures concerning discharge and framing charges. [3](https://www.mha.gov.in/sites/default/files/2024-04/250884_2_english_01042024.pdf#page=62) [4](https://www.mha.gov.in/sites/default/files/2024-04/250884_2_english_01042024.pdf#page=82)

A **court-framed charge** identifies the accusation to be tried at that stage. It is not a conviction.

## Release is not a verdict

**Bail** concerns release from custody subject to the applicable conditions and bond arrangement. A bail order is not an acquittal. Read the actual order rather than assuming that release proves either innocence or political favour. [5](https://www.mha.gov.in/sites/default/files/2024-04/250884_2_english_01042024.pdf#page=2)

## Read the outcome precisely

A **conviction** is a judicial finding of guilt. An **acquittal** is a judgment finding the accused not guilty in the proceeding. [6](https://www.mha.gov.in/sites/default/files/2024-04/250884_2_english_01042024.pdf#page=83) A **discharge** is a different procedural outcome, illustrated by the BNSS provisions dealing with whether sufficient grounds exist to proceed before framing a charge. [4](https://www.mha.gov.in/sites/default/files/2024-04/250884_2_english_01042024.pdf#page=82)

An **appeal** challenges a decision; filing it does not tell you its outcome. If an order stays a sentence or conviction, identify exactly what was stayed. Do not collapse every stay, discharge, withdrawal or quashing into the word “acquittal”.

## Preserve the case identity

Record the court, case number, relevant charge or proceeding, order date and current status date. Separate multiple proceedings involving the same person. Include a material later acquittal, reversal or correction where an earlier allegation was reported.

A historic election affidavit is not a substitute for this timeline. Nor does party membership establish political motive. Where the documents do not establish motive or current status, say so rather than filling in the gap.

articles.body_markdown:
A term is useful when it helps you understand a real question. These short definitions are entry points, not a replacement for the full article or the relevant legal text. Follow the linked explanation when the distinction matters.

## Country

India considered as a political and geographical community; not a synonym for the party in office. 

[Read the explanation](/in/start/country-state-government-party).

## State (in Article 12)

A defined constitutional term for Part III that includes specified governmental institutions and authorities. It is wider than one constituent state. [1](https://www.legislative.gov.in/static/uploads/2025/07/c9fe9c9b6840524844316f74bb1c556c.pdf#page=37)

[Read the explanation](/in/start/country-state-government-party).

## Government

Often the executive in office: ministers and the administration carrying out public decisions. Identify the institution when the word is being used more broadly. [2](https://www.legislative.gov.in/static/uploads/2025/07/c9fe9c9b6840524844316f74bb1c556c.pdf#page=65)

[Read the explanation](/in/start/country-state-government-party).

## Political party

A political organisation that may contest elections, govern, support a coalition or sit in opposition. It is not the same thing as the country. 

[Read the explanation](/in/start/politics-without-party-loyalty).

## Parliament

The constitutional institution consisting of the President, Rajya Sabha and Lok Sabha. [3](https://www.legislative.gov.in/static/uploads/2025/07/c9fe9c9b6840524844316f74bb1c556c.pdf#page=67)

[Read the explanation](/in/parliament/lok-sabha-rajya-sabha).

## Lok Sabha

The House of the People, with representatives elected from territorial constituencies. [3](https://www.legislative.gov.in/static/uploads/2025/07/c9fe9c9b6840524844316f74bb1c556c.pdf#page=67) [4](https://ncert.nic.in/textbook/pdf/keps203.pdf#page=6)

[Read the explanation](/in/parliament/lok-sabha-rajya-sabha).

## Rajya Sabha

The Council of States. Its elected state representatives are chosen by elected MLAs using the constitutional indirect-election method. [5](https://www.legislative.gov.in/static/uploads/2025/07/c9fe9c9b6840524844316f74bb1c556c.pdf#page=68)

[Read the explanation](/in/parliament/lok-sabha-rajya-sabha).

## MP

Member of Parliament. Specify the House and the role when assessing a particular action. [3](https://www.legislative.gov.in/static/uploads/2025/07/c9fe9c9b6840524844316f74bb1c556c.pdf#page=67)

[Read the explanation](/in/parliament/mp-role).

## MLA

Member of a Legislative Assembly. An Assembly and its state government are not interchangeable institutions. [6](https://www.legislative.gov.in/static/uploads/2025/07/c9fe9c9b6840524844316f74bb1c556c.pdf#page=106)

[Read the explanation](/in/states/mla-and-mlc).

## MLC

Member of a Legislative Council, in a state where that institution operates. Councils and Assemblies have different composition and powers. [6](https://www.legislative.gov.in/static/uploads/2025/07/c9fe9c9b6840524844316f74bb1c556c.pdf#page=106) [7](https://www.legislative.gov.in/static/uploads/2025/07/c9fe9c9b6840524844316f74bb1c556c.pdf#page=119)

[Read the explanation](/in/states/mla-and-mlc).

## Council of Ministers

The executive group of ministers headed by the Prime Minister at Union level. It is collectively responsible to Lok Sabha. [2](https://www.legislative.gov.in/static/uploads/2025/07/c9fe9c9b6840524844316f74bb1c556c.pdf#page=65)

[Read the explanation](/in/start/country-state-government-party).

## Collective responsibility

The constitutional responsibility of the Council of Ministers to the relevant directly elected House: Lok Sabha at Union level and the Legislative Assembly at state level. [2](https://www.legislative.gov.in/static/uploads/2025/07/c9fe9c9b6840524844316f74bb1c556c.pdf#page=65) [8](https://www.legislative.gov.in/static/uploads/2025/07/c9fe9c9b6840524844316f74bb1c556c.pdf#page=104)

[Read the explanation](/in/parties/opposition-role).

## Opposition

The political side outside the governing side that can scrutinise it and offer alternatives. This broad term is different from a formally recognised leadership office. 

[Read the explanation](/in/parties/opposition-role).

## Constituency

An electoral unit that returns a representative under the applicable system. Ordinary Lok Sabha constituency elections return one winner. [4](https://ncert.nic.in/textbook/pdf/keps203.pdf#page=6)

[Read the explanation](/in/elections/how-seats-are-won).

## First-past-the-post

A constituency voting system in which the candidate with the most votes wins; an absolute majority is not required. [4](https://ncert.nic.in/textbook/pdf/keps203.pdf#page=6)

[Read the explanation](/in/elections/how-seats-are-won).

## Electoral roll

The list on which an elector must be included for the relevant election. Possession of an identity card is not a substitute for inclusion. [9](https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2177191)

[Read the explanation](/in/elections/voter-registration).

## EPIC

Electors Photo Identity Card. Identification and inclusion on an electoral roll are separate requirements to check. [9](https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2177191)

[Read the explanation](/in/elections/voter-registration).

## Affidavit

A sworn statement. An election affidavit is a dated disclosure by a candidate, not a judicial finding that every allegation it records is proved. [10](https://myneta.info/)

[Read the explanation](/in/elections/candidate-affidavits).

## Bill

A legislative proposal before enactment. A vote in one House does not automatically mean every required stage has been completed. [11](https://sansad.in/rs/legislation/introduction) [12](https://www.legislative.gov.in/static/uploads/2025/07/c9fe9c9b6840524844316f74bb1c556c.pdf#page=79)

[Read the explanation](/in/parliament/bill-to-law).

## Act

An enacted law. For practical application, check its commencement provisions and any later changes as well as assent. [11](https://sansad.in/rs/legislation/introduction)

[Read the explanation](/in/parliament/bill-to-law).

## Money Bill

A constitutionally defined category with a special parliamentary procedure. A proposal is not a Money Bill merely because it has a financial cost. [13](https://www.legislative.gov.in/static/uploads/2025/07/c9fe9c9b6840524844316f74bb1c556c.pdf#page=80)

[Read the explanation](/in/parliament/bill-to-law).

## Panchayat

A rural local-government institution within the applicable constitutional and state-law arrangements. Do not assume identical powers everywhere. [14](https://www.legislative.gov.in/static/uploads/2025/07/c9fe9c9b6840524844316f74bb1c556c.pdf#page=154)

[Read the explanation](/in/states/union-state-local-powers).

## Municipality

An urban local-government institution whose actual powers must be established under the applicable law, not assumed from its location alone. [15](https://www.legislative.gov.in/static/uploads/2025/07/c9fe9c9b6840524844316f74bb1c556c.pdf#page=162)

[Read the explanation](/in/local/find-responsible-authority).

## Budget Estimate (BE)

A budget-stage estimate for the specified financial year, not expenditure already completed. [16](https://www.indiabudget.gov.in/doc/Key_to_Budget_Document_2026.pdf#page=2)

[Read the explanation](/in/money/estimates-revised-actuals).

## Revised Estimate (RE)

An updated estimate for the specified year. It is still distinct from final reported actual expenditure. [16](https://www.indiabudget.gov.in/doc/Key_to_Budget_Document_2026.pdf#page=2)

[Read the explanation](/in/money/estimates-revised-actuals).

## Actual expenditure

Expenditure reported for a completed period under the source’s accounting scope. It does not by itself establish a service outcome. [17](https://www.indiabudget.gov.in/doc/Budget_at_Glance/bag1.pdf#page=3)

[Read the explanation](/in/money/read-a-budget).

## Fiscal deficit

In the budget presentation, the gap between total expenditure and receipts other than borrowing, under the stated accounting definitions. [18](https://www.indiabudget.gov.in/doc/Budget_at_Glance/bag1.pdf#page=3)

[Read the explanation](/in/money/read-a-budget).

## CAG

Comptroller and Auditor General of India, the constitutional audit institution. An audit observation is not a criminal conviction. [19](https://www.legislative.gov.in/static/uploads/2025/07/c9fe9c9b6840524844316f74bb1c556c.pdf#page=99)

[Read the explanation](/in/money/audits-and-cag).

## RTI

Right to Information: access to information held by public authorities, subject to the applicable law. It is different from requesting a service repair. [20](https://cic.gov.in/sites/default/files/RTI-Act_English.pdf#page=7) [21](https://aiimsbhubaneswar.nic.in/wp-content/uploads/2025/05/31-1.pdf#page=5)

[Read the explanation](/in/action/rti-basics).

## CPIO

Central Public Information Officer, the designated information officer in the Central RTI process. A portal nodal officer and the CPIO are not necessarily the same role. [22](https://rtionline.gov.in/faq.php?pageid=c9f0f895fb98ab9159f51fd0297e236d)

[Read the explanation](/in/action/rti-central-or-state).

## Grievance

A complaint seeking attention to a problem, such as a public-service failure. Its appropriate route depends on the subject and authority. [23](https://pgportal.gov.in/)

[Read the explanation](/in/action/choose-a-route).

## Allegation

A claim that something happened or someone did something. The word alone establishes neither truth nor falsity. 

[Read the explanation](/in/crime/case-status-terms).

## Chargesheet

Common terminology for a police report following investigation in the relevant procedural setting. It is distinct from a court-framed charge. [24](https://www.mha.gov.in/sites/default/files/2024-04/250884_2_english_01042024.pdf#page=62) [25](https://www.mha.gov.in/sites/default/files/2024-04/250884_2_english_01042024.pdf#page=82)

[Read the explanation](/in/crime/case-status-terms).

## Bail

Release from custody under the applicable conditions and bond arrangement. It is not a judgment of acquittal. [26](https://www.mha.gov.in/sites/default/files/2024-04/250884_2_english_01042024.pdf#page=2)

[Read the explanation](/in/crime/case-status-terms).

## Discharge

A procedural outcome distinct from acquittal; the cited sessions-trial provisions concern whether there is sufficient ground to proceed before framing a charge. [25](https://www.mha.gov.in/sites/default/files/2024-04/250884_2_english_01042024.pdf#page=82)

[Read the explanation](/in/crime/case-status-terms).

## Numerator

The quantity above the division line: what is being counted in a fraction or rate. 

[Read the explanation](/in/evidence/percentages-and-denominators).

## Denominator

The quantity below the division line: the population or total against which the numerator is compared. 

[Read the explanation](/in/evidence/percentages-and-denominators).

## Percentage point

The arithmetic difference between two percentages. A rise from 20% to 25% is five percentage points. 

[Read the explanation](/in/evidence/percentages-and-denominators).

## Reference period

The time the evidence describes. It is not necessarily the year the report was published. 

[Read the explanation](/in/evidence/question-official-data).

## Labour force participation rate

People in the labour force as a share of the relevant population, using the survey’s definitions and reference period. [27](https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2246009&lang=1&reg=3)

[Read the explanation](/in/everyday/jobs-and-wages).

## Worker population ratio

Employed people as a share of the relevant population, under the stated survey measure. [27](https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2246009&lang=1&reg=3)

[Read the explanation](/in/everyday/jobs-and-wages).

## Unemployment rate

Unemployed people as a share of the labour force, not of the entire population. [27](https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2246009&lang=1&reg=3)

[Read the explanation](/in/everyday/jobs-and-wages).

## Primary source

The original record relevant to a claim, such as an order, dataset or recording. Being original does not make it complete or infallible. 

[Read the explanation](/in/reference/how-we-know).

## Corroboration

Additional evidence supporting a claim. Copies of one original story are not independent confirmations. 

[Read the explanation](/in/evidence/check-before-sharing).

## Inference

A conclusion drawn from evidence rather than a fact directly stated or observed. Make the reasoning and uncertainty visible. 

[Read the explanation](/in/start/reasonable-disagreement).

## Conflict of interest

A relationship or incentive that may affect a judgment. Document the relationship; do not treat its existence as automatic proof that every statement is false. 

[Read the explanation](/in/media/assess-a-news-report).

A claim should stand or fall on its evidence, not on whether its conclusion is politically convenient. This site's purpose is to help you inspect that evidence and understand the limits of a conclusion.

## Start with the source that can establish the claim

For what a law says, identify the actual legal text and its version. For a parliamentary answer, use the answer rather than a headline describing it. For a statistic, identify the population, reference period, unit and method.

“Official” is a source description, not a guarantee that every interpretation is correct. A ministry release can establish what the ministry reported. It does not automatically prove the success of its policy or explain every conflicting observation.

Independent work can also be a primary source. ADR's analysis of election affidavits is an independent analysis, not an official government or judicial classification. A publisher's own editorial standards establish its stated rules, not independent certification that every article follows them. [1](https://adrindia.org/sites/default/files/Lok_Sabha_Elections_2024_Criminal_and_Financial_background_details_of_Winning_Candidates_Finalver_English%20%281%29.pdf#page=6) [2](https://reutersagency.com/about/standards-values/)

## Keep different statements visibly different

A factual claim, an allegation, an inference, an opinion and a hypothetical teaching example need different treatment. A hypothetical is labelled so that it cannot quietly become a reported incident.

The same applies to data. An actual table value, a calculation using that value and a judgment about what it means are separate steps. The source link should make those steps easier to inspect, not merely decorate the page.

## Date the evidence

Each article in this content edition carries a research-check date. A report's publication date and reference period are stored separately where established. A document checked today can still describe events from several years ago.

A “checked” label describes work performed for this edition. It is not a guarantee of continuous monitoring or an assertion that no later correction exists. Historical legal compilations are labelled with their actual cutoffs instead of being silently presented as current consolidated law.

## Correct the claim, not only the spelling

When better evidence changes a conclusion, the correction should identify the original claim, the supporting record and the substantive change. Related summaries and charts need the same correction.

No anonymous guilt rankings, fabricated incidents or unsupported claims of political motive belong in this process. Where a source cannot establish the claim, the right result is a narrower statement or an explicit gap.

These articles received assistant source checks and calculation checks. They are not described as independently human-reviewed. Readers can use the linked records to examine or challenge the conclusions directly.

articles.body_markdown:
A crime statistic describes a defined set of recorded information. It is not automatically a count of every harmful event that occurred or every person who experienced harm.

Ask whether the source counts registered cases, victims, accused people, arrests, trials or outcomes. Those units cannot be substituted for one another.

## A real example of different categories

In an answer dated 12 August 2026, the Ministry of Road Transport and Highways distinguished 2024 road fatalities from deaths in a criminal negligence category. It reported 177,175 fatalities in the MoRTH series, 175,142 road-accident deaths in NCRB's accidental-death series and 162,500 deaths in the Crime in India negligence category. [1](https://sansad.in/getFile/annex/271/AU2820_vMN9Gb.pdf?source=pqars#page=1)

The answer explains differences in reporting channels and the scope of accidents versus offences recorded under penal law. The explanation is the Ministry's account; it is not an independent audit of the three full datasets. The figures nevertheless illustrate why a series title and definition matter. [2](https://sansad.in/getFile/annex/271/AU2820_vMN9Gb.pdf?source=pqars#page=2)

## A larger recorded count needs interpretation

In a **hypothetical district**, registered complaints rise after a reporting channel becomes easier to access. That rise alone cannot tell you how much underlying harm changed. You would need evidence about both events and reporting.

The reverse also needs care. A smaller recorded count is not automatic proof of improved safety. Do not invent a reporting explanation to dismiss a genuine deterioration either; investigate it.

## Do not mix a pipeline with a cohort

Suppose a hypothetical table reports cases registered during a year and convictions delivered during that year. The judgments may concern cases registered in earlier years. Dividing one by the other does not automatically produce the conviction rate for that year's new cases.

Read the publisher's stated denominator and follow the same cohort when that is the question you want to answer.

## “Political crime” needs a definition

An offence allegedly involving a politician, election violence and a claim of politically motivated prosecution are different categories. Decide what belongs in a collection and what evidence establishes a political connection.

Party affiliation alone does not establish motive. Nor does an accused person's assertion that a case is political settle whether the allegation is true or false.

Keep incident data, case status and interpretations of motive in separate fields. Where the underlying table or current proceeding cannot be verified, leave the claim unestablished rather than manufacturing a national total.

articles.body_markdown:
A difference between official figures deserves examination. Start by checking whether the sources actually count the same thing.

This example comes from **Rajya Sabha Unstarred Question 2820, answered on 12 August 2026** by the Ministry of Road Transport and Highways. The reference year is **2024**, not 2026. Both pages of the answer were inspected for this article. [1](https://sansad.in/getFile/annex/271/AU2820_vMN9Gb.pdf?source=pqars#page=1) [2](https://sansad.in/getFile/annex/271/AU2820_vMN9Gb.pdf?source=pqars#page=2)

## The figures given in the answer

| Series as described by the Ministry | 2024 figure | Category to preserve |
|---|---:|---|
| MoRTH Road Accidents in India | 177,175 | Total road-accident fatalities |
| NCRB Accidental Deaths and Suicides in India | 175,142 | Road-accident deaths in that series |
| NCRB Crime in India | 162,500 | Deaths due to negligence relating to road accidents |

These numbers are attributed to the Ministry's parliamentary answer. This article does not claim to have independently reconstructed all three underlying reports. [1](https://sansad.in/getFile/annex/271/AU2820_vMN9Gb.pdf?source=pqars#page=1)

## What the Ministry says explains the differences

The answer describes differences in state reporting channels and distinguishes accidental-death records from deaths recorded as penal-law offences. It also notes the accidental-death series' treatment of self-caused road accidents. These are the government's stated explanations, not a reason to stop asking methodological questions. [2](https://sansad.in/getFile/annex/271/AU2820_vMN9Gb.pdf?source=pqars#page=2)

The criminal negligence category should not be relabelled as an alternative count of every road fatality. A scope difference is not repaired by averaging the numbers.

## Question and answer are different evidence

A parliamentary question may contain a premise, an estimate or an allegation. Its appearance in an official document does not turn that premise into a finding by the government or Parliament.

Read the reply and check what it accepts, rejects, qualifies or leaves unanswered. This article uses the figures stated in the answer rather than repeating the question's framing as an established fact.

## What you can conclude

The answer records three distinct reported figures and offers an explanation of their differing scope or collection. You can reproduce the difference between the first two figures: `177,175 − 175,142 = 2,033`.

That calculation does not establish which series captures every real-world death, prove intentional manipulation or show that reconciliation has been completed. Those are additional questions requiring additional evidence.

This is a model for reading conflicting data: preserve the units and categories, attribute explanations and make unresolved questions visible.

articles.body_markdown:
The Union Budget at a Glance provides a useful exercise in reading financial claims. The table used here is PDF page 3, printed page 1. All amounts below are in **₹ crore**. These are the figures in that budget document, not a live expenditure dashboard. [1](https://www.indiabudget.gov.in/doc/Budget_at_Glance/bag1.pdf#page=3)

## Read the four columns

| Measure | 2024–25 Actuals | 2025–26 BE | 2025–26 RE | 2026–27 BE |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Total expenditure | 46,52,867 | 50,65,345 | 49,64,842 | 53,47,315 |
| Revenue expenditure | 36,00,914 | 39,44,255 | 38,69,087 | 41,25,494 |
| Capital expenditure | 10,51,953 | 11,21,090 | 10,95,755 | 12,21,821 |

Source: rows 9, 10 and 13 of the table. BE means Budget Estimates; RE means Revised Estimates. [1](https://www.indiabudget.gov.in/doc/Budget_at_Glance/bag1.pdf#page=3)

## One reproducible calculation

Comparing 2026–27 BE total expenditure with 2025–26 RE:

`(5,347,315 − 4,964,842) / 4,964,842 × 100 = approximately 7.70%`

A supported description is: **the proposed total expenditure in 2026–27 BE is about 7.70% above the 2025–26 revised estimate.**

It would be unsupported to replace that with “government services improved by 7.70%” or “actual expenditure has already risen by 7.70%”. Neither conclusion follows from these two inputs.

## Check the arithmetic before the interpretation

For each column, revenue expenditure plus capital expenditure equals total expenditure in this table. That is a useful consistency check, not proof that every underlying transaction or policy decision was correct.

The table preserves the document's reported precision. Its values should not be mixed with a differently rounded chart without explaining the rounding.

## Change the denominator, change the question

The previous year's original Budget Estimate and Revised Estimate are different comparison bases. Both can be relevant, but the caption must identify which was used. Do not switch between them to obtain the largest headline percentage.

Nor is this calculation adjusted for inflation, population or the composition of expenditure. Those would be separate analyses requiring additional inputs.

The downloadable data card accompanying this article includes integer inputs, row labels, units and calculation checks. It does not claim that a budget estimate is a completed service outcome.

articles.body_markdown:
“Unemployment is low” does not by itself tell you whether people earn enough, have stable hours or can find the work they want. Start with the statistic's definition and population.

MoSPI's PLFS release defines three distinct measures: labour force participation uses the labour force as a share of the relevant population; the worker population ratio uses employed people as a share of that population; unemployment uses unemployed people as a share of the labour force. [1](https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2246009&lang=1&reg=3)

## A hypothetical group of 100 people

Suppose 57 people are employed, three are unemployed and 40 are outside the labour force under the chosen definitions.

The labour force is 60. Participation is 60%, the worker population ratio is 57% and unemployment is `3 / 60 × 100 = 5%`. It is not 43% simply because 43 people are not classified as employed.

This is a teaching example, not a PLFS result. It shows why the denominator matters.

## A dated official example

For January–December 2025, MoSPI's annual PLFS release reports, for persons aged 15 and above under usual status (principal plus subsidiary), LFPR of 59.3%, WPR of 57.4% and UR of 3.1%. These are annual survey estimates with a specified age group and activity-status measure, not today's live employment reading. [2](https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2246009&lang=1&reg=3)

The release distinguishes usual status, based on a longer reference period, from current weekly status, based on the preceding seven days. Do not mix the measures in a trend without explanation. [1](https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2246009&lang=1&reg=3)

## Check whether the series changed

The same release explains the sampling redesign from January 2025 and warns about comparability with earlier estimates. Do not turn a before-and-after comparison into a precise claim about improvement while hiding that qualification. [3](https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2246009&lang=1&reg=3)

## Ask the next question about work

To evaluate the experience of working people, look for suitable evidence on earnings, hours, stability or other aspects of work. The employment-status percentage alone cannot establish all of those outcomes.

Likewise, your difficult job search does not by itself measure the national unemployment rate, while a national rate does not refute your experience. Your age group, location and kind of work may require a more relevant comparison.

A useful headline names the measure. A useful conversation then asks what the measure leaves out.

articles.body_markdown:
A Bill is a legislative proposal. An Act is an enacted law. To understand what changed, identify the exact text and the stage it has reached rather than relying on a headline saying a law was “approved”.

Rajya Sabha's official introduction explains the general process from Bill to enactment. The Constitution supplies the rules and exceptions that prevent this from being a single identical path for every Bill. [1](https://sansad.in/rs/legislation/introduction) [2](https://www.legislative.gov.in/static/uploads/2025/07/c9fe9c9b6840524844316f74bb1c556c.pdf#page=79)

## Follow the text, not only the title

For an ordinary parliamentary Bill, check introduction, consideration and passage in the Houses, including any amendments. Do not assume the version introduced is identical to the version passed.

A parliamentary committee may examine a Bill, but do not claim every Bill automatically receives the same committee process. Use the record for that particular proposal. [3](https://sansad.in/ls/faq)

If a headline says a Bill cleared one House, look for the other House's position and the applicable procedure. A party announcement or Cabinet decision is not a substitute for the parliamentary record.

## Special categories need their own rules

Money Bills have a defined constitutional meaning and a special procedure under Articles 109 and 110. Rajya Sabha's role includes recommendations within a 14-day period, which Lok Sabha may accept or reject. A Bill is not a Money Bill merely because its proposal would cost money. [4](https://www.legislative.gov.in/static/uploads/2025/07/c9fe9c9b6840524844316f74bb1c556c.pdf#page=80)

Do not apply that shortcut to an ordinary Bill or describe all financial legislation as though it necessarily follows the same procedure.

## Check assent and commencement separately

After the required legislative stages, check the assent and published Act. Then read its commencement clause. The date an Act receives assent and the date a particular provision comes into operation need not be the same; the Act may specify dates or require a notification. For example, section 1(3) of the original BNSS text provides for commencement by Central Government notification; this is an illustration of the distinction, not a claim about a new commencement event today. [5](https://www.mha.gov.in/sites/default/files/2024-04/250884_2_english_01042024.pdf#page=2)

For an actual current-law claim, retrieve the relevant notification, later amendment or order affecting operation. This article explains how to read the stages; it does not declare a named Bill currently enforceable.

## A hypothetical headline audit

“New rules apply from today” could be wrong even if the underlying Act has received assent. Ask which provision creates the rule, which commencement instrument applies and whether the announcement is reporting an effective rule or a future proposal.

The safe summary is exact: “The Bill passed this House on this date” or “this provision commenced under this notification”. Precision makes it harder to present an incomplete stage as a finished change in the law.

articles.body_markdown:
A source-linked website should be open to a source-linked correction. Finding an error is a reason to improve the record, not to defend a sentence because it has already been published.

## Describe the problem precisely

A useful correction identifies the article, the exact sentence or figure and the evidence that changes it. Include the original document, date and relevant page, table or section where possible.

You can prepare a correction in this format:

> Article and version: [title, URL and version]
>
> Claim to check: [exact sentence or figure]
>
> Supporting record: [original source and locator]
>
> Issue: [incorrect value, missing context, outdated status, unsupported interpretation or another specific problem]
>
> Proposed correction: [wording, or the uncertainty that should replace the claim]

This template does not require you to supply a personal political affiliation or expose sensitive documents publicly.

## Separate disagreement from an error

A disagreement about priorities may not be a factual correction. But an interpretation can still be misleading if it rests on a wrong number, omits decisive context or presents an allegation as a finding.

A broken source link also deserves attention. Replacing it requires checking the new document, not merely finding another URL with a similar title.

## Make substantive changes visible

A substantive correction should record what was wrong, what changed and when. Related charts, summaries and translations should be updated too. A quiet edit is insufficient when readers may have relied on a materially different claim.

A typo that does not change the meaning can be handled differently from a corrected case outcome or misreported statistic. The correction record should match the significance of the change.

## Keep the evidence trail

Preserve the earlier article version and the reason for the change in the site's version history. Do not preserve unnecessary private information merely to make an audit trail look complete.

A new report does not necessarily make a correctly dated historical figure false. The correction may instead be to label the reference period more clearly, add a newer edition or remove an unsupported claim that the old figure was “current”.

This content edition includes article versions and source references so a correction can be traced. The website's chosen submission channel and actual response history must be configured by its maintainer; this page does not promise that an unbuilt reporting system is already operating.

articles.body_markdown:
You do not need to support a political party to ask whether a public decision is justified. You also do not need to oppose everything a party does because you disagree with it on another issue.

The practical starting point is a question you can investigate: what was promised, who had the power to act and what happened?

## Separate the policy from the identity

Consider a **hypothetical transport proposal**. Ask which problem it addresses, how the service would operate, what it would cost and who would be excluded. You can assess those questions before deciding how the proposal fits your overall view of the party promoting it.

If the proposal involves public spending, use the actual budget-stage evidence. A proposed allocation and completed expenditure are different categories in the official budget documents. Treating them as interchangeable benefits a preferred party no more legitimately than an opposing one. [1](https://www.indiabudget.gov.in/doc/Key_to_Budget_Document_2026.pdf#page=2)

## Use the same test twice

Write a standard you would apply to an opponent: an original source for a figure, a clear account of costs or a current court record for a legal allegation. Then apply it to a politician you support.

Consistency does not mean giving each party equal praise and criticism. If the evidence differs, the conclusions may differ. Artificial balance would hide that difference rather than correct it.

## You are allowed to have priorities

You may value a policy's distributional effects differently from another reader. That is a reason to explain the trade-off, not to pretend your preference is a measured fact.

Ask which part of the disagreement could change with evidence and which part reflects different priorities. Evidence can establish who receives a benefit; it does not automatically determine how you should weigh every competing need.

## Keep a route back to revision

Write down what would change your assessment: a completed audit, a revised policy text or better delivery evidence. Then take that evidence seriously if it appears.

A change of mind is useful when it follows a corrected premise. There is no need to defend an old claim simply because people associate you with the side that made it.

Political awareness can begin as a practice of asking better questions, with no membership, public argument or declaration of loyalty required.

articles.body_markdown:
Two people can agree on a number and disagree about what should be done. They can also claim to disagree about values while relying on incompatible factual assumptions.

Separating these layers makes an argument easier to examine.

## What happened?

Start with checkable claims. Was money approved or spent? What does the report cover? What did the order actually decide?

For example, the Union Budget separately labels Budget Estimates, Revised Estimates and actuals. Two people using different columns may appear to disagree about a single amount when they are answering different questions. [1](https://www.indiabudget.gov.in/doc/Budget_at_Glance/bag1.pdf#page=3)

Resolve the definition and period before interpreting the difference.

## What might happen next?

A prediction needs assumptions. Ask what must be true for the proposed result to follow, what could change the outcome and how the prediction will be evaluated.

Do not present a forecast as an observed fact. Nor should the existence of uncertainty make every forecast equally plausible: compare the supporting evidence and reasoning.

## What should matter most?

In a **hypothetical bus-policy debate**, one person might prioritise lower fares while another prioritises increasing frequency within a constrained budget. Evidence about cost, usage and available capacity can inform the argument. A remaining disagreement may concern the weight each person gives to those goals.

Name that choice. “We disagree about which benefit should take priority” is clearer than accusing the other person of rejecting all evidence.

## Fairness is not false balance

Represent the opposing argument accurately, but do not give an unsupported claim equal standing simply to make the presentation symmetrical. A well-established fact and an unevidenced allegation need different treatment.

The same standard applies when one side is your own. A documented correction is not something to conceal because it weakens a preferred argument.

## End with the unresolved question

Sometimes agreement is unnecessary. You can establish which claims are supported, identify a genuine trade-off and leave the remaining judgment visible.

A useful closing sentence is: “We agree on these records, disagree about this consequence, and would need this evidence to test it.” That gives the conversation somewhere to go besides repeating labels.
